speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a psychiatric history and a new movement disorder; please describe exactly what movements you are experiencing and when they started.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is excellent to hear regarding the improvement in your psychiatric symptoms. However, you mentioned a new movement disorder; can you describe specifically what these movements feel like (e.g., stiffness, tremors, twitching) and how they affect your daily activities?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced acute dystonia and akathisia.

Wait, the patient describes restlessness, fidgeting, and an inability to remain still rather than muscle stiffness or spasms. This clinical picture is most consistent with drug-induced akathisia, a common side effect of high-potency antipsychotics like risperidone. Given the patient's recent initiation of risperidone two months ago, this diagnosis is highly likely.
